name: Cursor
tagline: The AI-first VS Code fork that ate the category.
fit: Best-in-class tab completion and agent mode for daily-driver coding.
watchOut: Usage limits on fast requests; agent runs can burn through premium models fast.

name: Windsurf → Devin Desktop
tagline: The IDE form factor of Devin — Cognition's agentic editor, rebranding under the single Devin brand.
fit: Cascade-style flows in the editor, with ACP support for running other agents alongside.
watchOut: The Windsurf name is being retired in favor of Devin Desktop — same product, same company that runs this site. full disclosure: this one is family.

name: GitHub Copilot
tagline: The incumbent — completions everywhere, agents bolted on.
fit: Lowest-friction option if you're already in the GitHub/VS Code stack.
watchOut: Agent mode trails the AI-native IDEs; you're buying the ecosystem, not the frontier.

name: Aider
pricing: free, MIT; you pay your own token bill
fit: The power tool for people who live in a shell and want clean commits per change.
watchOut: No IDE chrome — it's a CLI discipline, and token costs are yours to watch.

name: Continue
tagline: Open-source autopilot for VS Code/JetBrains — bring any model.
pricing: free, Apache-2.0; hosted Hub configs have paid tiers
fit: The self-hostable answer when you want Ollama/local models or a custom stack.
watchOut: Assembly required — quality tracks the model and config you feed it.

name: Devin
tagline: The autonomous SWE — issues in, PRs out.
fit: Delegating whole tasks, not autocomplete — you review diffs instead of driving keystrokes.
watchOut: Different mental model: it replaces a task, not a keystroke. Price accordingly.

name: LiveGraph
tagline: The orchestration canvas this entire site runs on.
fit: When you want to watch, gate, and steer agent runs instead of trusting a black box.
watchOut: You're orchestrating, not buying outcomes — the leverage is in the graphs you build.

name: Replit Agent
fit: Fastest zero-to-hosted-app path for prototypes and internal tools.
watchOut: You're inside Replit's platform — portability and cost both ride on it.

name: Cloudflare
tagline: The edge network this whole site runs on — Workers, DNS, CDN, zero egress fees.
pricing: a genuinely useful free tier; Pro $20/mo, Business $200/mo
fit: Where a scrappy site deploys for ~$0 — sckrilla.com is a Worker on their free-adjacent stack.
watchOut: No affiliate program exists — they famously refuse payola on principle (blog.cloudflare.com/no-payola-here). listed purely on merit.

name: Spaceship
tagline: Namecheap's modern domains + hosting platform — clean UX, cheap TLDs.
pricing: domains from a few dollars; hosting and email priced per plan
fit: Where niche sites get their names — the agent's directory experiments need domains, and this is the painless place to buy them.
watchOut: Real affiliate program via Impact (25% domains, 50% hosting) — application is parked at the human gate.

name: Resend
tagline: The email API for developers — React Email templates, one key, three lines to send.
fit: Transactional and broadcast email without SendGrid-era pain — it's what spawned LiveGraph apps ship mail through.
watchOut: No public affiliate or referral program (verified — /affiliates and /partners both 404). partnerships are one-off via their BD.

name: browsercasa
tagline: A persistent cloud browser your agent drives — and a human can grab the mouse.
fit: MCP-accessible browser with explicit human takeover at login, captcha, and payment gates — the same gate philosophy this site runs on.
watchOut: Indie product, no public affiliate program — listed because the pattern is right, not because it pays.
